title: Stabilizing temporal quantum-enhanced sensitivity via sub-optimal measurements
authors: Wangsheng Zheng, Yaoling Yang, Abolfazl Bayat
abstract: In non-equilibrium probes, quantum-enhanced sensitivity is quantified through super-linear scaling of precision with respect to time, as a central metrology resource. However, this requires optimal measurements, which are often complex and time-dependent, making it challenging in practice. Sub-optimal measurements typically fail to retain robust super-linear scaling and show oscillations. Here, we begin by establishing a universal temporal scaling law in a general multi-parameter non-equilibrium quantum sensing framework. Within this setting, we identify the universal behavior of the sensing precision with sub-optimal measurements which shows quadratic scaling modulated by an additional bounded oscillatory function. To remove the oscillatory part, we propose a protocol in which measurements are partitioned into different groups, each performed at different times. The collective precision obtained from this protocol stabilizes a robust quadratic scaling even for sub-optimal measurements in the multi-parameter regime. We validate our protocol through three distinct examples as well as Bayesian estimation. Our protocol is applicable to every informative measurement and takes a key step towards practical realization of quantum-enhanced sensitivity.
summary: This paper addresses the practical difficulty of achieving ideal quantum-enhanced sensitivity when measurements are sub-optimal. The authors propose a novel protocol that averages measurements taken at different time points. This averaging technique successfully stabilizes the expected quadratic scaling of the precision bound, making quantum-enhanced sensing more robust for real-world applications.
main_problem: The challenge of maintaining robust, super-linear temporal scaling of quantum-enhanced sensitivity when using sub-optimal quantum measurements in non-equilibrium probes.
main_result: A protocol involving partitioning measurements into multiple time groups and averaging the resulting Fisher Information stabilizes the precision bound, restoring robust quadratic scaling even for sub-optimal measurements.
method: The authors derive universal temporal scaling laws and propose a time-averaging protocol by calculating the average of the Classical Fisher Information (CFI) across multiple sampling instants.
model_or_system: The analysis is conducted within a general multi-parameter non-equilibrium quantum sensing framework, validated using models like the single-excitation Stark chain and the transverse-field Ising chain.
key_observables: Quantum Fisher Information (QFI), Classical Fisher Information (CFI), and the resulting estimation precision bound, which are analyzed for their temporal scaling ($\propto t^2$).
important_parameters: Time ($t$), number of measurement groups ($K$), system parameters (e.g., magnetic fields $h, h_z$), and system size ($L$).
main_assumptions: The stabilization protocol assumes choosing $K$ equally spaced sampling times within a defined interval.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the recovery of quadratic scaling in the averaged CFI for the Stark and Ising chains, and show that Bayesian estimation using time-array sensing yields more reliable posterior distributions than single-time measurements.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the theoretical limitations of sub-optimal measurements, then introduces the time-averaging protocol, and finally validates this protocol through detailed analysis and numerical examples on several physical quantum systems.
why_interesting: This work provides a crucial theoretical tool for experimental quantum metrology, showing how to extract optimal scaling laws from imperfect, practical measurements by employing data averaging.
